question: A number of publications have reported that the EU is looking into suspicions of corruption in six funding award processes. The reports are currently before the Spanish courts and have also been referred to the European Public Prosecutor’s Office and the European Anti-Fraud Office (case OC/2022/0892). The investigation is looking into roughly EUR 500 million that could have been granted to the Barcial del Barco and La Robla biorefinery project. 1.
What precautionary measures has the Commission taken following the allegations of fraud under investigation?
How many millions of euros were awarded to the Barcial del Barco and La Robla biorefinery, and who were the beneficiaries?
Does the Commission know whether the funds from this project are being channelled into other industrial projects in La Robla?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (12.4.2024) 1. As part of its mandate to protect the financial interests of the Union, the European AntiFraud Office (OLAF) analyses incoming information of potential investigative interest to determine whether there are sufficient grounds to open an investigation.

Specialised experts evaluate this information to find out whether it falls within OLAF’s competence to act and whether there is a sufficient suspicion of fraud, corruption or any illegal activity affecting the EU’s financial interests. OLAF can confirm that it received allegations concerning the two projects mentioned by the Honourable Member.

Following an analysis of the allegations, OLAF decided not to open an investigation into the matter. In order to comply with its legal and operational obligations, OLAF cannot share further details. 2. The Commission does not have information on EU support to the Barcial del Barco and La Robla biorefinery. 3.
The Commission does not have information on whether funds are being channelled into other industrial projects in La Robla.
